nodes.title: A. Food delivery
key_items: Food rescue; Food on train; Scheduled orders; Group ordering
nodes.summary: Zomato's B2C food delivery platform connects customers with local restaurants and independent delivery partners for on-demand ordering and last-mile delivery across 800+ Indian cities. FY25 metrics include 853 million orders (13% YoY growth), INR 32,862 crore NOV (20% growth), 20.6 million average monthly transacting customers (12% growth), 473k average monthly active delivery partners (18% growth), INR 385 net AOV (6% growth), and 297k average monthly active restaurant partners (20% growth). The Zomato Gold membership program had 12.1 million active members. New initiatives included food rescue, food on train with IRCTC, scheduled orders, group ordering, and Zomato for Enterprise. Zomato Legends and Zomato Everyday were discontinued.

nodes.title: B. Quick commerce
nodes.summary: Blinkit is a quick commerce B2C marketplace offering on-demand delivery via a network of stores within 2-3 km and a last-mile fleet. It delivers products across categories like daily essentials, electronics, beauty, home décor, toys, and general merchandise. FY25 key metrics include INR 22,371 crore NOV (113% YoY growth), 10.2 million average monthly transacting customers (100% YoY growth), 424 million orders (108% YoY growth), 1,301 stores (775 net new), Net AOV of INR 528 (2% YoY growth), and presence in 100+ cities (70+ new). The fiscal saw rapid geographic expansion with new stores in unserved localities and high-demand areas, plus investment in backend warehousing, totaling 5.2 million sq ft as of Mar-25. Assortment expanded to include protein supplements, guitars, skipping ropes, keyboards, dumbbells, geysers, curtains, coolers, tables, laptops, air conditioners, yoga pants, TVs, gym wear, smartphones, shoes, music instruments, electronics, gym essentials, apparel, home decor, and home appliances.

nodes.title: C. Going-out

It outlines dining-out discovery/reservations, movie ticketing partnerships, sports ticketing (including exclusive IPL team inventory), and event ticketing. FY25 metrics include NOV of INR 6,618 crore (156% YoY growth), NAOV of INR 1,906 (28% YoY growth), 34.7 million transactions (4x YoY growth), and 14.0 million District app downloads. Highlights list specific partnerships and events like Diljit Dosanjh's tour, Feeding India Concert, Pushpa 2, Dining Carnival, IPL 2025 (1.1 million tickets sold), Zomaland, and other concerts and matches.

nodes.title: íá Climate conscious deliveries
nodes.summary: The text outlines climate-conscious delivery goals: achieving Net Zero emissions by 2033, maintaining zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions (achieved in FY25 via offsets and IRECs), and reducing last-mile emissions by 70% per km by FY30 from FY22 base. In FY25, last-mile emissions fell 10.5% through EV initiatives, with 37k EV delivery partners, 88 million EV deliveries, and ~5k tonnes CO2e avoided; the goal is 100% EV deliveries by 2030 under EV100. A responsible sourcing policy evaluates suppliers on energy and emissions. Subsidiaries show increased EV adoption: 15,000+ active EV quick commerce partners, 31% EV-based Hyperpure deliveries (up from 20%), and a 300 KVA solar plant generating 4 lakh units annually.

nodes.title: Waste free world
nodes.summary: The text outlines waste reduction initiatives in FY25, including the 'Don’t send cutlery' option defaulted on over 75% of orders, preventing ~1,057 MT of cutlery waste, and 100% plastic neutral deliveries via recycling 15,000 MT of plastic waste (45,000 MT total). New initiatives are the 'Food Rescue' program, rescuing ~30% of cancelled orders (~200,000 kg food waste prevented), and the 'Zomato plastic-free future' program, tagging 7,500+ restaurants for low plastic packaging. Additionally, subsidiary Hyperpure delivered 2,700 MT of sustainable packaging to 47,000+ restaurant outlets.

nodes.title: ÔÏ Zero hunger
nodes.summary:
ÔÏ Zero hunger
Feeding India (FI), a Zomato giveback, continued to progress on its mission to make India malnutrition free. Through its Daily Feeding Program, FI provides nutritious meals daily to over 100,000 children in under-served communities, reaching more than 1,000 educational centres across 160+ cities. FI served 36 million meals in FY25 and more than 200 million meals overall since inception.
In Dec-24, FI hosted its second edition of the Zomato Feeding India Concert headlined by international singer Dua Lipa. This concert was organized to raise awareness around the cause of eliminating hunger and malnutrition in India and was attended by an audience of 25,000+ people.

nodes.title: éÏ Health, safety & wellbeing for all
nodes.summary:
éÏ Health, safety & wellbeing for all
We continued to progress towards on-road safety for delivery partners and expanded the reach of our ‘first-responder training program’. Under this initiative, delivery partners are trained in medical first aid and CPR through professional and certified training programs to act as emergency first responders in case of on road casualties. Such timely interventions can potentially save lives of all road users. As of Mar-25, we had trained ~52k delivery partners under this initiative.
Even across our key subsidiaries, in our quick commerce and Hyperpure businesses, we trained 190k store workers and 59k warehouse workers on safety guidelines and procedures including fire safety, ergonomics and electrical risks.

nodes.title: Customer Experience | Governance
nodes.summary: The text covers four governance areas: Customer Experience, Technology, People Management, and Business Strategy. For Customer Experience, it outlines risks like service unavailability and failure to adapt to preferences, mitigated through partner training, support teams, and product expansion. Technology discusses cybersecurity threats and measures including dedicated teams, advanced tools, bug bounty programs, and training. People Management addresses talent retention and succession risks, with initiatives for diversity, employee wellness, mentorship, and recognition. Business Strategy notes risks of revenue stagnation without innovation and store management, though mitigation details are cut off.

nodes.title: Eternal's Technology Governance and People Management Social Overview
nodes.summary: The text covers Eternal's customer-centric approach, expanding product categories and features, and strategic efforts to be a one-stop solution. It details technology and governance, focusing on cybersecurity threats, dedicated teams, governance frameworks, advanced tools, regular testing, bug bounty programs, training, and system upgrades for business continuity. It also addresses people management and social aspects, including challenges in talent retention and succession planning, competitive benefits, diversity and inclusion policies, parental leaves, wellness programs, mentorship, succession planning, and reward programs to build an inclusive workforce.

nodes.title: Business Strategy | Governance
nodes.summary: The text outlines Eternal's risk of revenue stagnation and constrained growth due to lack of strategy for product innovation, technological advancement, and store management, leading to over-reliance on limited revenue streams and missed opportunities. It then describes Eternal's commitment to stakeholder experience through innovation and new product development, using feedback and rigorous testing. To mitigate over-reliance, Eternal has diversified across verticals like Hyperpure, District, and Blinkit. Finally, it states that by embedding innovation, expanding markets, and scaling agility, Eternal is positioned for growth and long-term value.

nodes.title: Competition | Governance
nodes.summary: The text addresses competitive and governance risks, including potential negative impacts from new entrants and existing rivals, such as pricing pressures, higher acquisition costs, and challenges in differentiation and loyalty. It highlights mitigation through a diversified high-growth portfolio, investments in research, technology, and data insights, and a focus on customer service, stakeholder relationships, and retention. The company leverages execution capabilities via differentiated products, marketing, and operational efficiencies. It monitors market dynamics to recalibrate strategies, prioritizes talent and cross-functional capabilities, and commits to long-term brand building through responsible, customer-first marketing and educational campaigns to reinforce trust and engagement.

nodes.title: Stakeholder Management | Governance
nodes.summary: Eternal identifies risks from ineffective stakeholder management, including revenue loss, operational disruption, and reputational damage due to delivery partner strikes, artist or sponsor cancellations, supply chain interruptions, vendor departures, and service discrepancies. To mitigate these, Eternal has dedicated support teams for each stakeholder group, proactive relationship management, and targeted initiatives to attract, retain, and empower stakeholders. It forecasts stakeholder needs to secure availability and minimize disruptions, ensuring service continuity. The company also commits to stakeholder well-being through insurance for delivery partners, health and safety training for delivery partners and third-party manpower. Eternal views stakeholders as the backbone of its business and aims to create a supportive, rewarding, and sustainable ecosystem for mutual growth.

nodes.title: Macro economics | Social & Governance
nodes.summary: Eternal faces revenue and growth risks from macroeconomic fluctuations and geopolitical volatility, which can affect interest rates, inflation, consumer confidence, demand, costs, and market certainty. To mitigate, Eternal diversifies across verticals, price points, and spending capacities, reducing reliance on a single segment. Its Quick Commerce essential goods business sustains demand during downturns. Eternal also monitors short- and long-term trends, adapting strategy through product launches, modifications, and resource reallocation. Diversification, continuous analysis, and strategic agility build resilience against uncertainties, supporting sustained growth in challenging environments.

nodes.title: 17. Internal financial controls and their adequacy
nodes.summary: The text covers the Company's internal financial controls as part of its risk and governance framework, addressing financial and operational risks. It details the controls' purpose: adherence to policies, asset safeguarding, fraud prevention, accurate accounting, and timely financial reporting. The Company has implemented adequate controls over financial reporting, ensuring transactions are authorized, recorded, and reported correctly, complying with accounting standards. Key controls are documented, automated, and embedded in business processes. Assurance to the Board is through three lines of defense: management reviews, continuous monitoring by the Governance, Risk and Compliance Function, and independent testing by Statutory and Secretarial Auditors. The Company has an Equal Parental Leave Policy extended to both male and female employees which is in compliance to the Maternity Benefit Act 1961. Beyond leave, we support employees through access to mental wellness programs, professional counseling, and structured return-to-work programs that ease the transition back to their roles with confidence. The consolidated financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss, changes in equity, cash flow) with comparatives for March 31, 2025 and 2024 are presented, including auditors' and directors' signatures.

nodes.title: D. We have indicated to the auditors and the audit committee:
nodes.summary: The text includes three annexures from Eternal Limited's financial report. Annexure VII is a CEO/CFO compliance certificate under SEBI Regulation 17(8), certifying review of financial statements for FY2024-25, no fraudulent transactions, responsibility for internal controls, and disclosure of no significant changes in internal controls or accounting policies and no significant fraud. Annexure VIII is a declaration by the CEO confirming compliance with the Code of Conduct by the board and senior management for FY2024-25. It also begins the Independent Auditor's Report on the Consolidated Financial Statements to the members of Eternal Limited.

nodes.title: Opinion
nodes.summary: The section covers the auditor's opinion on Eternal Limited's consolidated financial statements for FY 2024-25, stating they give a true and fair view under Ind AS, with an emphasis on GST orders and four key audit matters: fair valuation of investments, revenue recognition, goodwill impairment, and business combination. It outlines responsibilities of management and the board for financial statements and internal financial controls, and the auditor's responsibilities including risk assessment, going concern evaluation, and communication with governance. Other matters note reliance on other auditors for nine subsidiaries and one trust, and unaudited financial information for twelve subsidiaries. The report on legal and regulatory requirements includes CARO reporting, audit trail deficiencies, and internal financial controls opinion. Annexures detail internal financial controls, their meaning, inherent limitations, and the auditor's unmodified opinion on their adequacy and effectiveness.

nodes.title: Auditor's Opinion, Basis, Emphasis of Matter, and Key Audit Matters
nodes.summary: The text presents an auditor's opinion on the consolidated financial statements of Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato Limited) and its subsidiaries and trust for the year ended March 31, 2025. It states that the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards. The Basis for Opinion section describes the audit's compliance with Standards on Auditing, independence, and sufficiency of audit evidence. The Emphasis of Matter highlights Note 38(a) regarding GST orders on delivery charges, where the company believes it has a strong case, and the opinion is not modified. Key Audit Matters are introduced as matters of most significance in the audit, with details to follow.

nodes.title: Key Audit Matters
nodes.summary: This independent auditor's report for Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato Limited) covers the audit of consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes the opinion that the statements give a true and fair view, the basis for opinion, an emphasis of matter regarding GST on delivery charges, and four key audit matters: fair valuation of investments in other entities, revenue recognition, impairment assessment of goodwill, and business combination. For each key audit matter, the auditor describes the matter and the principal audit procedures performed.

nodes.title: Information Other than the Financial Statements and Auditor’s Report Thereon
nodes.summary: The text outlines the auditor's responsibilities regarding information other than the financial statements and auditor's report. It states that the Parent's Board of Directors is responsible for the other information, which comprises the Board report but excludes the financial statements and auditor's report. The auditor's opinion does not cover this other information. The auditor's responsibility is to read the other information when available, compare it with the financial statements and the work of other auditors, consider material inconsistencies or misstatements, and rely on other auditors' work for subsidiaries and trust. If a material misstatement is found in the Board report, the auditor must communicate it to those charged with governance per SA 720.

nodes.title: Responsibilities of Management and Board of Directors for the Consolidated Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The text outlines management and board responsibilities for consolidated financial statements under section 134(5) of the Act, including preparation that gives a true and fair view of financial position, performance, cash flows, and equity per Ind AS. It details responsibilities for maintaining accounting records, safeguarding assets, preventing fraud, selecting accounting policies, making judgments and estimates, and ensuring effective internal financial controls. It also covers assessing going concern, disclosing related matters, and using the going concern basis unless liquidation or cessation is intended. Finally, it notes the board's responsibility for overseeing the financial reporting process.

nodes.title: Auditor’s Responsibility for the Audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The text outlines the auditor's responsibilities for auditing consolidated financial statements, including objectives of obtaining reasonable assurance and issuing an opinion. It details procedures: identifying and assessing risks of material misstatement from fraud or error, understanding internal financial controls (and opining on their adequacy and effectiveness under the Act), evaluating accounting policies and estimates, assessing going concern, evaluating overall presentation and disclosures, and obtaining sufficient evidence for group entities including coordination with other auditors. It discusses materiality in planning and evaluation, communication with governance about audit scope, findings, independence, and key audit matters.

nodes.title: Other Matters
nodes.summary: The text addresses two 'Other Matters' regarding unaudited components in consolidated financial statements. It states that the auditor did not audit the financial statements of 9 subsidiaries and 1 trust (total assets ₹2,174 crores, revenues ₹349 crores, net cash inflows ₹23 crores), which were audited by other auditors, and the opinion relies solely on their reports. It also notes that the financial information of 12 subsidiaries (total assets ₹101 crores, revenues ₹14 crores, net cash inflows ₹2 crores) is unaudited, furnished by management, and the opinion relies solely on such information; these are deemed not material to the Group. The auditor's opinion and report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements are not modified regarding these matters.

nodes.title: Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
nodes.summary: The text is an auditor's report on compliance with legal and regulatory requirements for a group's consolidated financial statements. It covers: obtaining necessary information; maintaining proper books despite audit trail non-compliance; agreement of financial statements with books; Ind AS compliance; director disqualification; internal financial controls (unmodified opinion); director remuneration compliance; audit trail deficiencies (database-level log retention limits, third-party software lacking SOC reports, but no tampering found); pending litigations disclosure; no foreseeable losses or IEPF transfers; no fund advances/loans with ultimate beneficiary arrangements and no material misstatements; no dividends declared; accounting software audit trail exceptions and preservation of prior year logs; CARO reporting with qualifications for eight subsidiaries under Clause 3(xvii); and Annexure A on internal financial controls responsibilities and auditor's opinion.

nodes.title: Auditor's Annexure on Internal Financial Controls
key_items: Annexure “A” to the Independent Auditor’s Report

Management’s and Board of Directors’ Responsibilities for Internal Financial Controls

nodes.title: Auditor’s Responsibility
nodes.summary: The text outlines the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion on internal financial controls over financial reporting for the Parent and its Indian subsidiary companies, based on an audit conducted per ICAI Guidance Note and Standards on Auditing under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013. It details audit procedures, including understanding controls, assessing material weakness risks, and testing design and operating effectiveness. The evidence obtained, including from other auditors, is deemed sufficient. It defines internal financial controls, notes inherent limitations like collusion or management override, and provides an opinion that controls were adequate and operating effectively as of March 31, 2025. Other Matters clarify reliance on subsidiary auditors' reports, without modifying the opinion, and the report is signed by Deloitte Haskins & Sells.

nodes.title: Internal Financial Controls: Meaning and Inherent Limitations
key_items: Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with reference to consolidated financial statements
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with reference to consolidated financial statements
nodes.summary: The page defines internal financial controls for consolidated financial statements as processes providing reasonable assurance of reliable financial reporting under GAAP, including policies for accurate recordkeeping, authorized transactions, and prevention of unauthorized asset use. It also outlines inherent limitations, noting that collusion, management override, errors, or fraud may cause undetected material misstatements, and that future evaluations risk becoming inadequate due to changing conditions or declining compliance.

nodes.title: Opinion
nodes.summary: The text includes an auditor's opinion on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal financial controls for the Parent and its Indian subsidiaries, referencing reliance on other auditors for nine subsidiaries. It then presents the consolidated financial statements: balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, statement of changes in equity, and cash flow statement, all with comparative figures for March 31, 2025 and 2024. The balance sheet details assets, equity, and liabilities; the profit and loss statement shows income, expenses, profit, and earnings per share; the equity statement reconciles share capital and other equity; and the cash flow statement reports operating activities. Signatures of auditors and directors are included.

nodes.title: B) Cash flows from investing activities
nodes.summary: The text presents the consolidated statement of cash flows for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering investing and financing activities, net cash changes, and cash composition. Investing activities list purchases and sales of property, plant, equipment, bank deposits, mutual funds, businesses, non-current investments, government securities, debentures, loans, and interest received, with comparative figures. Financing activities include equity issuance, borrowing repayments, share issue costs, ESOP-related transactions, lease payments, and interest paid. It shows net cash increase/decrease, foreign exchange differences, and beginning/ending cash balances. Cash equivalents comprise bank balances, short-term deposits, and cash on hand. The document includes auditor and board signatures, dates, and a reference to material accounting policies.

nodes.title: 1. Corporate Information
nodes.summary: The text covers the corporate information of Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato Limited), including its incorporation, listing, registered office, and name change. It describes the Group's e-commerce platforms for food delivery, quick commerce, ingredient supply, and services like entertainment ticketing, delivery, warehousing, and dining out. It notes the acquisitions of Orbgen Technologies and Wasteland Entertainment in August 2024. It also covers the basis of preparation and measurement of consolidated financial statements, including compliance with Ind AS, historical cost basis with exceptions at fair value, presentation in Indian Rupees rounded to crores, and the basis of consolidation, including control assessment and uniform accounting policies.

nodes.title: Investment in associates Associate
nodes.summary: The section covers accounting for investments in associates using the equity method, including initial recognition at cost, share of profits/losses and OCI, goodwill, impairment, and loss of significant influence. It details use of estimates and critical judgments, business combinations and goodwill using the acquisition method, current/non-current classification, foreign currency translation, fair value measurement hierarchy, property plant and equipment depreciation, goodwill and intangible asset amortization and impairment, lease accounting for lessees, inventories valuation, revenue recognition across e-commerce and related services, contract balances, employee benefits, income taxes, share-based payments, segment reporting, earnings per share, treasury shares via employee benefit trust, provisions and contingent liabilities, financial instruments classification and impairment, events after the balance sheet date, and fair value measurement of financial instruments.

nodes.title: Investment in associates Associate (intro)
nodes.summary: The text defines an associate as an entity with significant influence but not control, and details the equity method for accounting investments in associates. It covers initial recognition at cost, adjustments for share of net assets, goodwill inclusion, recognition of share of profits/losses and OCI, elimination of unrealized gains/losses, and treatment of losses exceeding interest. It also addresses consistency of reporting periods and accounting policies, impairment assessment, and measurement upon loss of significant influence.

nodes.title: a) Use of estimates
nodes.summary: The text outlines the use of estimates in preparing consolidated financial statements under Ind AS, requiring management to make judgments, estimates, and assumptions that affect reported amounts of revenues, expenses, assets, liabilities, and contingent liability disclosures. It notes that these estimates are based on current knowledge but may require material future adjustments due to uncertainty. Estimates and underlying assumptions are reviewed on an ongoing basis, with revisions recognized in the year of revision or in both current and future years if applicable. Significant areas of estimation, uncertainty, and critical judgments are disclosed in note 2.4.

nodes.title: b) Business combination and goodwill
nodes.summary: The text covers two accounting policy areas. First, business combinations (except common control) using the acquisition method: acquisition cost measured as fair value of consideration plus non-controlling interests; identifiable assets and liabilities recognized at acquisition-date fair values, including contingent liabilities regardless of probability; election to measure non-controlling interests at fair value or proportionate share; expensing acquisition-related costs except debt/equity issuance costs under Ind AS 32/109; and classification/designation of acquired financial assets and liabilities based on contractual terms and conditions at acquisition date. Second, current versus non-current classification in the consolidated balance sheet, listing criteria for current assets (realization/consumption in operating cycle, held for trading, realization within twelve months, unrestricted cash equivalents) and current liabilities (settlement in operating cycle, held for trading, due within twelve months, no unconditional deferral right), noting deferred tax items are non-current and defining the operating cycle as twelve months.

nodes.title: d) Foreign currencies
nodes.summary: The text covers the Group's accounting policies for foreign currencies, including the presentation currency (INR) and functional currency determination. It details initial recording of foreign currency transactions using spot or average rates, translation of monetary assets and liabilities at reporting date spot rates, recognition of exchange differences on monetary items in profit and loss, and translation of non-monetary items at historical rates. It also addresses foreign operations: on consolidation, assets and liabilities are translated at reporting date rates, while income and expenses use transaction-date or average rates, with translation differences recognized in OCI and reclassified to profit and loss on disposal.

nodes.title: e) Fair value measurement
nodes.summary: This text defines fair value as the price in an orderly market transaction, assuming sale in the principal or most advantageous accessible market. It covers measurement using market participant assumptions, including highest and best use for non-financial assets. The Group uses appropriate valuation techniques maximizing observable inputs. All fair value measurements are categorized into a three-level hierarchy (Level 1: quoted prices; Level 2: observable inputs; Level 3: unobservable inputs). For recurring measurements, transfers between hierarchy levels are assessed at each reporting year-end. Disclosure classes are determined by nature, characteristics, risks, and hierarchy level.

nodes.title: f) Property, plant and equipment
nodes.summary: This text outlines the accounting policy for property, plant and equipment (PPE), covering initial measurement at cost including directly attributable expenditures, and subsequent costs capitalization criteria. It addresses capital work in progress, depreciation methods (straight-line) with useful lives per Schedule II and management estimates for various asset classes, and amortization of leasehold improvements. It also covers management's estimation and annual review of useful lives and residual values, pro-rata depreciation for assets purchased during the year, full depreciation of low-cost assets (below ₹5,000), and derecognition principles including gain/loss treatment.

nodes.title: g) Goodwill and other intangible assets
nodes.summary: This policy covers goodwill and intangible assets. Goodwill is the excess of acquisition cost over fair value of net assets, tested annually for impairment. Intangible assets acquired separately are initially measured at cost; those from business combinations at fair value. Subsequently, they are carried at cost less amortization and impairment. Internally generated intangibles (except capitalized development costs) are expensed. Useful lives are finite or indefinite. Finite-lived software and websites are amortized straight-line over 1-3 years. Impairment is assessed when indicators exist; useful lives and amortization methods are reviewed annually, with changes treated as estimates. Amortization is recognized in profit or loss. Derecognition occurs on disposal or when no future benefits are expected, with gains/losses in profit or loss. Intangible assets from business combinations (brand, customer contracts, technology platform, content/reviews, trademarks, restaurant listing platform, non-compete, domain/website, merchant relationship) are amortized straight-line over specified lives (2-10 years).

nodes.title: h) Leases
key_items: Lease liabilities; Short term leases and leases of low value assets
Short term leases and leases of low value assets
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Group's lease accounting policy, covering the assessment at contract inception to determine if a contract is or contains a lease. It details the lessee approach: recognition of lease liabilities and right-of-use (ROU) assets, excluding short-term and low-value leases. It describes ROU asset initial measurement (including lease liabilities, direct costs, and incentives), subsequent depreciation over the shorter of lease term or useful life, and impairment. Lease liabilities are measured at present value of lease payments using the incremental borrowing rate, with subsequent interest accretion, payments, and remeasurement triggers. It also covers expense recognition for short-term and low-value leases. The text mentions the Company's office premises leases with terms of 1 to 9 years.

nodes.title: i) Inventories
nodes.summary: This section covers material accounting policies, including inventories valued at lower of cost (FIFO) and net realizable value. Revenue recognition policies detail e-commerce platform services, event management, traded goods, warehousing, and ancillary services, with specific principles for food delivery, quick commerce, advertisement, subscriptions, delivery facilitation, ticketing, and event organization. Contract balances (contract assets, trade receivables, contract liabilities) and employee benefits (defined contribution and defined benefit gratuity plans, compensated absences) are addressed. Tax policies include current tax measurement, recognition outside profit or loss, and offsetting, plus deferred tax recognition and measurement. Share-based payments, segment reporting, earnings per share, and treasury shares are also covered.

nodes.title: i) Inventories (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines two accounting policies: inventories and revenue recognition. Inventories are valued at lower of cost (FIFO, including purchase price, taxes, freight, and incidental costs) and net realizable value (estimated selling price less costs to sell). Revenue recognition covers the Group's e-commerce platform services, event management, traded goods, warehousing, and ancillary services. Revenue is measured at transaction price net of taxes and discounts, recognized over time or at a point in time when control transfers. Specific principles are detailed for food delivery and quick commerce (identifying customers, principal vs. agent, commission income, user incentives, platform fees), advertisement revenue (recognized over contract period or when clicks/impressions assured are met), and subscription revenue (recognized over subscription period on a systematic basis).

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition Policies for Platform Transactions
key_items: Food delivery and quick commerce transactions:
nodes.summary: The text outlines revenue recognition principles for a group operating e-commerce platforms, covering food delivery and quick commerce. It defines customer identification based on service provision and consideration, identifying restaurant/quick commerce merchants as customers, and users as customers only under specific delivery or service fee conditions. It details commission income recognition from merchants on a point-in-time basis, treatment of user incentives as revenue netting or expenses depending on customer status, platform fee revenue recognized when services are rendered, and advertisement revenue recognized over contract periods or when assured clicks/impressions are met.

nodes.title: Subscription revenue
nodes.summary: The text outlines revenue recognition policies: subscription revenue recognized systematically over the subscription period; sign-up revenue from partners recognized on receipt or over time; delivery facilitation services where the Group acts as a platform provider and recognizes fees at a point in time; delivery services where the Group is responsible and recognizes delivery fees at a point in time; warehousing services recognized when control transfers to the customer; sale of traded goods recognized upon transfer of control, including non-cash consideration; ticketing services where the Group acts as an agent and recognizes net commission and convenience fee at a point in time; event organization and management services with own events recognized at a point in time and third-party event management recognized over time based on completion; interest income using the effective interest rate method; and contract assets recognized when a conditional right to consideration exists.

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition Policies for Various Services
nodes.summary: The text outlines revenue recognition policies for sign-up revenue from partners, delivery facilitation and delivery services, warehousing services, sale of traded goods, ticketing services (net commission and convenience fee), event organisation and management services (own events recognized at a point in time and third-party event management over time), and interest income using the effective interest rate method.

nodes.title: Contract balances: Contract assets
nodes.summary: The text covers key accounting policies: contract assets (right to consideration conditioned on future performance), trade receivables (unconditional right to payment), and contract liabilities (obligation to transfer goods/services for received consideration). It also details employee benefits: defined contribution plans (provident fund/social security) with expense recognition and liability/asset adjustments; defined benefit gratuity plans in India and UAE using the projected unit credit method, with reimbursement rights from insurance products measured at fair value, remeasurements in OCI, and expense components (service costs and net interest). Finally, it addresses compensated absences, noting liabilities for earned leaves not wholly settled within 12 months are measured at present value.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Trade Receivables, Contract Liabilities, and Employee Benefits
nodes.summary: The text covers material accounting policies: trade receivables as unconditional rights to consideration; contract liabilities for obligations to transfer goods/services when consideration is received; retirement benefits including defined contribution provident fund/social security with expense recognition and asset/liability adjustments, and foreign contributions per local laws; and defined benefit gratuity plans in India and UAE using the projected unit credit method, with plan assets as reimbursement rights under Ind AS 19, remeasurements in OCI, and expense recognition for service costs and net interest.

nodes.title: Compensated Absences
nodes.summary:

nodes.title: l) Taxes Current tax
nodes.summary:
l) Taxes Current tax
Current tax assets and liabilities are measured at the amount expected to be recovered from or paid to the taxation authorities. The tax rates and tax laws used to compute the amount are those that are enacted or substantively enacted, at the reporting date in the countries where the Group operates and generates taxable income.
Current tax relating to items recognized outside consolidated profit and loss is recognized outside consolidated profit and loss (either in other comprehensive income or in equity). Current tax items are recognized in correlation to the underlying transaction either in OCI or directly in equity. Management yearly evaluates positions taken in the tax returns with respect to situations in which applicable tax regulations are subject to interpretation and establishes provisions where appropriate.
Advance taxes and provisions for current taxes are presented in the consolidated balance sheet after off-setting advance tax paid and income tax provision arising in the same tax jurisdiction and where the relevant tax paying unit intends to settle the asset and liability on a net basis.

nodes.title: Deferred taxes
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for deferred taxes, share-based payments, segment reporting, earnings per share, and treasury shares. Deferred tax recognition and measurement rules for temporary differences, including exceptions, are detailed. Share-based payment policies describe equity-settled transactions, valuation, expense recognition, modifications, and dilution effects. Segment reporting defines operating segments and lists five segments with descriptions. Earnings per share calculation for basic and diluted EPS is explained. Treasury shares via an Employee Benefit Trust are mentioned.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Segment Reporting and Earnings Per Share
nodes.summary: The page details material accounting policies for segment reporting and earnings per share. It defines operating segments as components regularly evaluated by the CODM (CEO and Managing Director) for resource allocation and performance assessment, listing five segments: India food ordering and delivery, Hyperpure supplies (B2B), Quick commerce, Going Out, and All other segments (residual), with descriptions of each. It explains that directly attributable revenue and expenses are reported under each segment, while indirect expenses are allocated based on orders, employees, or gross market value. For earnings per share, it outlines basic EPS calculation (net profit attributable to equity shareholders divided by weighted average equity shares) and diluted EPS adjustments for all dilutive potential equity shares. It also notes that dilutive options increase share dilution in diluted EPS and that modifications increasing fair value or benefiting employees are measured at modification date.

nodes.title: p) Treasury shares
nodes.summary:
p) Treasury shares
The Group has created an Employee Benefit Trust (EBT). The Group uses EBT as a vehicle for distributing shares to employees under the employee stock option

Own equity instruments that are held by the trust are recognized at cost and deducted from equity. No gain or loss is recognized in consolidated statement of profit and loss on the purchase, sale, issue, or cancellation of the Group’s own equity instruments. Any difference between the carrying amount and the consideration, if reissued, is recognized in other equity.

nodes.title: q) Provisions and contingent liabilities Provisions
nodes.summary: The section covers accounting policies for provisions, contingent liabilities, and financial instruments. Provisions are recognized for present obligations when reliable estimates are possible and outflow is probable, with discounts for material time value effects. Contingent liabilities are disclosed but not recognized. Financial assets are initially recognized at fair value plus transaction costs (except FVTPL) and classified into amortised cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL based on the SPPI test and business model. Derecognition occurs when rights expire or risks and rewards are substantially transferred. Impairment uses expected credit loss models: simplified approach for trade receivables and general approach for other financial assets. Financial liabilities are initially measured at fair value and subsequently at amortised cost or FVTPL. Offsetting requires legal right and intention to net settle. Non-financial asset impairment is assessed with recoverable amount as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments with maturities of three months or less.

nodes.title: Contingent liabilities
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for provisions, contingent liabilities, and financial instruments. Provisions are recognized for present obligations from past events when a reliable estimate is possible and resource outflow is probable, with expenses reported net of reimbursements; material time value effects are discounted using a pre-tax rate reflecting liability risks, and the unwinding discount is a finance cost. Contingent liabilities are possible obligations from past events confirmed by uncertain future events, or present obligations not recognized due to improbable outflow or unreliable estimation, and are disclosed but not recognized. Financial instruments are defined as contracts creating a financial asset for one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument for another.

nodes.title: Financial assets Initial recognition and measurement:
nodes.summary: The text details the accounting treatment of financial assets under Ind AS 109. It covers initial recognition and classification into amortised cost, FVTOCI, and FVTPL, based on contractual cash flow characteristics (SPPI test) and the business model. Initial measurement includes fair value plus transaction costs (except for FVTPL). Regular way trades are recognized on trade date. Subsequent measurement for debt instruments is explained for each category, including interest income, impairment, and derecognition treatment. Equity instruments are measured at FVTPL unless an irrevocable election is made for FVTOCI, with no recycling of gains/losses on derecognition. The Group has elected FVTOCI for certain equity and preference instruments not held for trading. The document also includes company information and material accounting policies for the year ended March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: Derecognition
nodes.summary: The text outlines the derecognition criteria for financial assets: when rights to cash flows expire, or when rights are transferred or a pass-through arrangement exists and either substantially all risks and rewards are transferred, or control is transferred. It details the evaluation of retained risks and rewards, and if neither transferred nor retained substantially nor control transferred, continued recognition to the extent of continuing involvement with an associated liability measured to reflect retained rights and obligations. Guarantees are measured at the lower of original carrying amount and maximum consideration repayable.

nodes.title: Impairment of financial assets
nodes.summary: The text covers impairment of financial assets, detailing the Group's forward-looking expected credit loss (ECL) assessment for amortised cost and FVTOCI debt instruments, with different methodologies based on significant increase in credit risk. For trade receivables and contract assets, the simplified approach under Ind AS 109 recognizes lifetime ECL from initial recognition using a provision matrix adjusted for forward-looking factors. For other financial assets, 12-month ECL is used unless credit risk increased significantly, then lifetime ECL; reversals occur if credit quality improves. ECL is recognized in profit or loss. It also covers financial liabilities: initial recognition and measurement at fair value, classification as amortised cost or FVTPL, subsequent measurement using EIR method or fair value, derecognition, and offsetting of financial instruments. Finally, it addresses impairment of non-financial assets, including assessment of indications and determination of recoverable amount as higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities Accounting Policies
key_items: Financial liabilities Initial recognition and measurement
Financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for financial liabilities. It covers initial recognition at fair value, classification for subsequent measurement at amortised cost or fair value through profit or loss, and notes that the Group's liabilities include trade payables, lease liabilities, and other financial liabilities. Subsequent measurement details amortised cost using the effective interest rate method, with gains/losses in profit or loss, and fair value through profit or loss for held-for-trading or designated liabilities, including treatment of own credit risk changes in OCI. Finally, derecognition criteria are explained, including discharge, cancellation, expiration, and substantial modifications treated as derecognition of the original liability with differences in carrying amounts recognized in profit or loss.

nodes.title: Offsetting of financial instruments
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies on offsetting financial instruments, impairment of non-financial assets, and cash and cash equivalents. It details offsetting criteria based on legal right and net settlement intention. For impairment, it explains assessment timing, recoverable amount determination (fair value less costs of disposal and value in use), impairment loss recognition and allocation (including goodwill to CGUs), annual testing for goodwill, and reversal conditions. Cash equivalents are defined as short-term, highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, and for cash flow purposes, net of bank overdrafts.

nodes.title: u) Events occurring after the balance sheet date
nodes.summary: The text covers two main areas: events after the balance sheet date and estimates and critical judgements. It explains the distinction between adjusting and non-adjusting events, with adjustments made for adjusting events that provide additional information about conditions at the balance sheet date, while non-adjusting events may be disclosed. It then discusses estimates and critical judgements, noting they are continuously evaluated based on historical experience and assumptions, with actual results potentially differing materially. Changes in estimates are recognized when known. Specifically, it addresses defined benefit plans (gratuity benefits), which use actuarial valuations involving assumptions such as discount rate, future salary increases, and mortality rates. The discount rate is most subject to change and is based on government bond interest rates, while mortality rates use publicly available tables, and salary increases are based on expected inflation.

nodes.title: Fair value measurement of financial instruments
key_items: Impairment of Goodwill; Control and significant influence assessment; User incentives
nodes.summary: The text covers fair value measurement of financial instruments using valuation techniques when quoted prices are unavailable, including inputs, estimates, and judgments related to liquidity risk, credit risk, and volatility. It discusses goodwill impairment testing annually or upon indication, involving significant estimates of future economic and market conditions. Critical judgments in accounting policies include control and significant influence assessment, and accounting for user incentives (as revenue reduction or advertising expense). Deferred tax recognition requires judgment on future taxable profits. Property, plant and equipment and intangible assets/goodwill notes show gross carrying values, additions, disposals, business combinations, depreciation/amortization, impairment, and net block as of March 31, 2025, with comparatives.

nodes.title: i. Use of estimates
nodes.summary: The text outlines three accounting policy areas: use of estimates, business combinations and goodwill, and current versus non-current classification. It explains that management makes judgments, estimates, and assumptions affecting reported amounts, which are reviewed and revised with prospective or current-year recognition. Business combinations (except common control) use the acquisition method, measuring consideration and non-controlling interests at fair value, recognizing identifiable assets and liabilities at acquisition-date fair values, and expensing acquisition costs except security issuance costs. Assets and liabilities are classified as current based on operating cycle, trading, twelve-month realization/settlement, or unrestricted cash, with all others non-current; deferred taxes are always non-current, and the operating cycle is twelve months.

nodes.title: iv. Foreign currencies
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for foreign currencies, specifying the Company's functional currency as Indian rupees. It covers translation of foreign operations' financial statements using their functional currency, initial recording of foreign currency transactions at spot or average rates, and translation of monetary assets/liabilities at reporting date spot rates with exchange differences recognized in profit and loss. Non-monetary items at historical cost use initial transaction rates. For consolidation, foreign operations' assets/liabilities are translated at reporting date rates, income/expenses at transaction date or average rates, with exchange differences in OCI, reclassified to profit and loss on disposal.

nodes.title: v. Fair value measurement

Finally, it addresses goodwill and other intangible assets: goodwill impairment testing, initial and subsequent measurement, useful life assessment (finite or indefinite), amortization of software/websites (1–3 years), impairment review, derecognition, and amortization of business-combination intangibles (technology platform and trademarks, 5 years).

nodes.title: viii. Leases
key_items: Right-of-use assets; Lease liabilities; Short-term leases and leases of low-value assets
Short-term leases and leases of low-value assets

It details the recognition and measurement of right-of-use assets, including initial measurement at cost, depreciation over the shorter of lease term and useful life, and impairment. It also covers lease liabilities, including initial measurement at present value of lease payments using the incremental borrowing rate, subsequent measurement with interest accretion, and remeasurement triggers. Inventories are valued at lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost is determined on first in first out basis. Inventory cost includes purchase price and other directly attributable costs (such as taxes other than those subsequently recovered from the tax authorities), freight inward and other related incidental expenses incurred in bringing the inventory to its present condition and location.
Net realisable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less estimated cost necessary to make the sale.

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition for E-Commerce Platform Services
key_items: Service provided by restaurant partners and commission income:
nodes.summary: The page covers revenue recognition principles, including the company's main revenue from e-commerce platform services to restaurant partners, plus advertisement, subscription, and ancillary services. Revenue is measured at transaction price net of taxes, discounts, and rebates, including non-cash consideration. Revenue is recognized over time or at a point in time when control transfers. It details food delivery transactions with separate contracts for users, restaurant partners, and delivery partners. Customer identification criteria: restaurant partners are customers; users are customers only if charged a service fee; users are not customers of restaurant partners. The company acts as principal only when controlling goods or services, concludes it does not control restaurant partners' goods/services, and recognizes commission income from restaurant partners at a point in time.

nodes.title: User incentives
nodes.summary: The text covers user incentives accounting (netted against revenue or expensed), revenue recognition policies for platform services (recognized at point in time), advertisement revenue (over contract period and upon meeting click/impression assurances), subscription revenue (systematically over subscription period), sign-up revenue (on receipt or over time per agreement), delivery facilitation services (point-in-time fee), and interest income (using effective interest rate method). It also details contract balances: contract assets (conditional rights), trade receivables (unconditional rights), and contract liabilities (obligations for consideration received). Finally, it discusses retirement and other employee benefits, specifically defined contribution schemes like provident fund and social security, with expense recognition when service is rendered and liability recognition for deficits.

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition Policies and Contract Balances
nodes.summary: The text outlines revenue recognition policies for platform services, advertisement, subscription, sign-up, and delivery facilitation services, along with interest income. Platform fees are recognized at a point in time, advertisement revenue over contract periods or upon meeting click/impression guarantees, subscription revenue systematically over the subscription period, sign-up amounts on receipt or over time per agreements, and delivery facilitation fees at a point in time. Interest income uses the effective interest rate method. It also covers contract assets (conditional rights to consideration) and trade receivables (unconditional rights).

nodes.title: Contract liabilities
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for contract liabilities, retirement and other employee benefits including defined contribution schemes (provident fund, social security, foreign branch contributions) and defined benefit plans (gratuity in India and UAE using projected unit credit method, reimbursement rights, remeasurements in OCI), compensated absences measured using projected unit credit method, and current tax measurement and recognition.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Defined Benefit Plans and Compensated Absences
nodes.summary: This document outlines accounting policies for defined benefit plans (gratuity) and compensated absences. For defined benefit plans, it covers the projected unit credit method, reimbursement rights, remeasurements in OCI, and expense recognition. For compensated absences, it addresses measurement of earned leave liabilities using actuarial present value and recognition of remeasurements in profit and loss. The text also includes a brief header referencing the company overview and statutory reports.

nodes.title: xii. Taxes Current tax
nodes.summary: This policy outlines current tax accounting: measuring assets and liabilities at expected amounts using enacted or substantively enacted rates and laws in operating countries. It addresses recognition of current tax outside profit or loss (in other comprehensive income or equity for related items), management's yearly evaluation of uncertain tax positions and establishment of provisions, and balance sheet presentation of advance taxes and current tax provisions net of offsetting within the same tax jurisdiction where net settlement is intended.

nodes.title: Deferred taxes
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for deferred taxes and share-based payments. Deferred tax is calculated on temporary differences between tax bases and carrying amounts, with detailed recognition criteria and exceptions for deferred tax liabilities and assets, including initial recognition exceptions and investments in subsidiaries. It addresses review, measurement at expected tax rates, recognition outside profit or loss, and offsetting criteria. Share-based payment policy covers equity-settled transactions, measurement at grant-date fair value, expense recognition over vesting period, treatment of performance and non-vesting conditions, modifications, and dilutive effect on earnings per share.

nodes.title: xiv. Earnings per share
nodes.summary:
xiv. Earnings per share
Basic earnings per share are calculated by dividing the net profit or loss for the year attributable to equity shareholders by the weighted average number of equity shares.
For the purpose of calculating diluted earnings per share, the net profit or loss for the year attributable to equity shareholders of the Company and the weighted average number of shares outstanding during the year are adjusted for the effects of all dilutive potential equity shares.

nodes.title: xv. Provisions and Contingent liabilities Provisions
nodes.summary: The section outlines accounting policies for provisions, contingent liabilities, and financial instruments. Provisions are recognized for present obligations when outflow is probable and estimable, with discounting and net reimbursements. Contingent liabilities are disclosed but not recognized. Financial instruments are initially classified at amortized cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL based on cash flow characteristics and business model, with initial measurement at fair value plus transaction costs (except FVTPL). Subsequent measurement of debt instruments depends on classification. Equity instruments are measured at FVTPL unless irrevocable election for OCI. Derecognition occurs when rights expire or transfer with risks/rewards evaluation. Impairment uses expected credit losses with simplified approach for trade receivables. Financial liabilities are classified at amortized cost or FVTPL, with derecognition and offsetting rules. Non-financial assets are assessed for impairment.

nodes.title: xv. Provisions and Contingent liabilities Provisions (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for provisions, contingent liabilities, and financial instruments. Provisions are recognized for present obligations from past events when outflow is probable and estimable, with expenses net of reimbursements and discounting for time value. Contingent liabilities are possible obligations from past events confirmed by uncertain future events or present obligations not recognized due to improbability or unreliable estimation, and are disclosed only. Financial instruments are contracts creating financial assets/liabilities or equity. Financial assets are initially classified at amortized cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL based on cash flow characteristics and business model. Initial measurement is at fair value plus transaction costs (except FVTPL). SPPI test determines classification. Business model determines if cash flows come from collecting, selling, or both. Regular way trades are recognized on trade date. Subsequent measurement of debt instruments depends on business model and cash flow characteristics, with three measurement categories.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Contingent Liabilities and Financial Assets
key_items: Financial assets Initial recognition and measurement:
nodes.summary: The page covers material accounting policies for the year ended March 31, 2025. It first addresses provisions, noting that reimbursements are presented net in profit and loss, and that material provisions are discounted using a pre-tax rate reflecting risks, with the unwinding of discount recognized as a finance cost. It then defines contingent liabilities as possible obligations confirmed only by uncertain future events or present obligations not recognized due to improbability or unreliable estimation, and states they are disclosed not recognized. Next, it introduces financial instruments and details initial recognition and measurement of financial assets: classification at amortised cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL based on contractual cash flow characteristics (SPPI test) and business model; initial measurement at fair value plus transaction costs except for FVTPL (costs expensed) and trade receivables without significant financing component (at transaction price); and trade-date recognition for regular way trades.

nodes.title: Subsequent Measurement Debt instruments
nodes.summary: The text details subsequent measurement of financial instruments under Ind AS 109. Debt instruments are classified into three categories based on business model and cash flow characteristics: amortised cost (for held-to-collect assets with solely principal and interest cash flows, with interest income using EIR, and gains/losses on derecognition and impairment in profit or loss), FVTOCI (for held-to-collect-and-sell assets, with fair value movements in OCI except impairment, interest, and foreign exchange in profit or loss, and cumulative gains/losses reclassified to profit or loss on derecognition), and FVTPL (for assets not meeting criteria, with all fair value changes, interest, dividends, and foreign exchange in profit or loss). Equity instruments are measured at FVTPL unless an irrevocable election is made on an instrument-by-instrument basis to present fair value changes in OCI (if not held for trading), with no subsequent reclassification to profit or loss on derecognition, and dividends recognized in profit or loss. The Company has made such an irrevocable election for certain equity and preference instruments not held for trading.

nodes.title: Derecognition

Finally, it addresses financial liabilities: initial recognition at fair value, classification for subsequent measurement at amortised cost or fair value through profit or loss, and subsequent measurement at amortised cost for liabilities like trade payables and lease liabilities.

nodes.summary:
(c) Financial risk management Financial risk factors
The Company’s activities exposes it to a variety of financial risks namely market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. The Company’s primary focus is to foresee the unpredictability of financial markets and seek to minimise potential adverse effects on its financial performance. Risk management is carried out by senior management for cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables, investments, deposits with banks, foreign currency risk exposure and liquidity risk.
Market risk
Market risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices. Market risk comprises three types of risk: interest rate risk, foreign currency risk and other price risk, such as equity price risk and commodity risk. The Company ensures optimisation of cash through fund planning and robust cash management practices.
